setup.pitch: Rosebridge's Festival of Bonds honors every chosen connection in town. This year organizers kept only romantic ribbons—and the Heartloom has begun tying people together against their will.
setup.gmSummary: The Heartloom is an old enchanted loom beneath Rosebridge used during the Festival of Bonds. Traditionally townsfolk tie ribbons naming any meaningful bond: siblings, friends, teachers, partners, teammates, caretakers. This year festival chair Celia Thorn narrowed the public display to romantic pairs to make the event more marketable. Hundreds of friendship, family, and mentorship ribbons were boxed away. The Heartloom responds by trying to 'complete' the missing pattern literally: glowing cords bind strangers, pull separated people together, and distort the bridge. The party must discover what was removed, recover the boxed ribbons, help several affected relationships speak for themselves, and decide whether Rosebridge restores the broad tradition, replaces the magical loom with a voluntary civic ritual, or cuts the enchantment entirely.
setup.background: Rosebridge was founded by refugees who survived because unrelated households chose to become kin. The Heartloom was woven to celebrate chosen bonds, not romance specifically. Over centuries the festival became increasingly decorative. Celia Thorn, hoping to turn it into a destination event, redesigned the display around couples and quietly stored all other ribbons in the guild archive. The loom interprets those omissions as broken strands and begins physically forcing connections to fill the gaps.
setup.campaignFrame: Maestra Vell brings a Hearthford student delegation to Rosebridge's Festival of Bonds and calls on the party when the Heartloom begins forcing labels onto people. The party returns to Hearthford with Vell remembering whether they defended self-defined bonds and consent.

quest.objective: Stop the Heartloom from forcing bonds, recover what was removed from the ritual, and decide what Rosebridge's Festival of Bonds should honor.
quest.stakes: People are being physically bound, old friendships are being misread as romance, family ties are being excluded, and the bridge structure is tightening under magical strain.
quest.deadline: FIVE KNOTS: show five knot marks. Fill one after the bridge, ribbon archive, three-way bond dispute, and underbridge loom approach; the fifth fills at the finale. Each knot increases forced-binding pressure.
successConditions: The missing ribbon categories are recovered or deliberately accounted for.
The Heartloom stops binding people without consent.
The party resolves the festival through Restore, Reweave, or Cut.
failureConditions: The party abandons Rosebridge while people remain magically bound.
The Heartloom is destroyed without releasing the bound crowd or documenting the erased bonds.

facts.text: The original Festival of Bonds honored friendship, family, mentorship, partnership, and other chosen ties—not only romance.
Celia Thorn ordered non-romantic ribbons removed from the public Heartloom display.
The Heartloom is trying to replace omitted relationships by physically binding people, not creating genuine affection.
A bond only stabilizes the loom when the people involved freely name it; forced pairings make the strain worse.
The crisis can end by restoring the broad ribbon pattern, replacing the Heartloom with a voluntary public bond registry, or cutting the enchantment.

scenes.title: Wrongly Tied
scenes.purpose: Launch the forced-bond crisis, show consent matters, and establish the five-knot clock.
scenes.readAloud: Rosebridge glows with hundreds of red ribbons when the first scream rises. A cord snaps out of a decorative arch and loops around two strangers' wrists. Another yanks a brother and sister toward a banner marked SWEETHEARTS. Beneath your feet, the stone bridge gives a low grinding groan. Five glowing knots appear along the central rail.
gmNotes: Show FIVE KNOTS. Fill 1/5 when this scene ends.
A bound pair can each use an Action to state their real relationship; if both freely agree on the label, their cord loosens automatically.
DC 13 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) can physically separate a forced cord long enough to move, but it reforms unless the relationship is accurately named or the source is fixed.
Celia sends the party to the archive to find out why the display pattern is incomplete.
Do not treat magical pairing as proof of attraction or consent.

runSteps.title: Demonstrate voluntary naming

scenes.title: Boxes of Missing Bonds
scenes.purpose: Prove the broad original tradition and expose the deliberate removal of non-romantic ribbons.
scenes.readAloud: The Ribbon Guild archive smells of dust, lavender, and hot wax. Five colored shelves line the wall—but four are nearly empty. On the floor, sealed boxes are labeled FRIEND, FAMILY, MENTOR, and CHOSEN KIN. A sponsor poster leans against them: ROSEBRIDGE — THE CITY OF PERFECT PAIRS.
gmNotes: Fill FIVE KNOTS 2/5 when the party leaves.
No roll is needed to see excluded ribbon categories.
DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation or History) reconstructs the founder pattern from old plans. Failure costs time but the tapestry and shelf labels reveal the same five categories.
The signed transfer list and sponsor brief establish Celia's decision without requiring confession.
Recovering and sorting the boxes gives advantage on the first Restore action in the finale.

runSteps.title: Open the boxes

runSteps.title: Show the old pattern

runSteps.title: Preserve proof

exitChoices.label: Test the truth in Bond Square

scenes.title: Say What We Are
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate consent mechanically and humanize different bond types before the finale.
scenes.readAloud: Bond Square has become a web. A grandmother is tied to her apprentice. Two former partners are pulled face-to-face while both shout no. Juniper Vale and Tomas Reed stand wrist-to-wrist under a glowing label that reads PARTNER. Juniper looks at the label, then at you. “We are best friends. Start there.”
gmNotes: Fill FIVE KNOTS 3/5 after three bond examples are resolved.
Resolve three examples: friendship, family/mentorship, and a bond that should be released rather than relabeled.
For each example, both affected people freely naming the same real relationship releases or stabilizes the cord automatically.
DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) can calm bystanders long enough to let affected people speak. Failure adds one STRAIN mark but nobody is forced to declare a relationship.
Never require characters or NPCs to confess romance. 'No bond / release us' is a valid outcome when both people reject the connection.

runSteps.title: Run three different bond cases
runSteps.text: Friendship, family/mentor, and release demonstrate the full rule.

runSteps.title: Let people name themselves
runSteps.text: Players facilitate; they do not decide other people's relationships.

runSteps.title: Watch the bridge
runSteps.text: Each accurate voluntary label visibly reduces local strain.

scenes.advanceWhen: Three examples prove the consent rule and Tomas opens the underbridge service route.

exitChoices.label: Go below the bridge
exitChoices.description: Reach the Heartloom through the service walk before the structure tightens further.

scenes.title: The Bridge Pulls Inward
scenes.purpose: Add physical stakes, expose the incomplete pattern, and make preparation affect the final encounter.
scenes.readAloud: Below the festival music, the bridge sounds like a ship in ice. Glowing cords pass through cracks in the stone and pull toward the central arch. Four channels in the old masonry are dark. Only the PARTNER channel burns bright enough to hurt your eyes.
gmNotes: Fill FIVE KNOTS 4/5 when the party reaches the chamber door.
Cross two tightening cord zones. DC 13 Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics); failure deals 1d6 force damage and Restrains the character until they or an ally spend an Action to free them.
Placing one recovered ribbon bundle into a dark channel disables that channel's hazard and grants one prepared Restore success in the finale, maximum 2.
The inscription CHOSEN WORD, CHOSEN STRAND is physical proof of consent.
If STRAIN is 2+, one bridge stone falls each round in the finale as difficult terrain; nobody is killed offscreen.

runSteps.title: Make the missing pattern physical
runSteps.text: Four dark category channels lead directly to the Heartloom.

runSteps.title: Reward recovered ribbons
runSteps.text: Using them here reduces finale work.

runSteps.title: Keep failure positional
runSteps.text: Cord zones restrain and damage but never seal the route.

scenes.advanceWhen: The party opens the Heartloom chamber with at least one legal resolution understood.

exitChoices.label: Enter the Heartloom chamber
exitChoices.description: Restore, reweave, or cut the festival's magic.

scenes.title: Restore, Reweave, or Cut
scenes.purpose: Resolve the holiday through broad inclusion, voluntary civic replacement, or ending the enchantment.
scenes.readAloud: The fifth knot ignites above the loom. Hundreds of ribbons whip through the chamber, weaving and unweaving names faster than you can read them. Three bronze shuttle handles rise from the frame: RESTORE PATTERN. REWEAVE RULE. CUT THREAD. The loom speaks in a hundred borrowed voices: “Name strand.”
gmNotes: The Heartloom has AC 15 and 70 HP if attacked; it is a magical object/construct-like hazard, not a creature with emotions.

RESTORE: reinsert five bond categories. Two may already be prepared from underbridge channels. Each remaining Action uses DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana/History), Wisdom (Insight), or Charisma (Persuasion/Performance) while placing a recovered ribbon bundle and naming the category's equal standing. Three total Restore successes after prepared successes end the crisis.

REWEAVE: establish three voluntary rules—self-named bonds only, opt-out/release always valid, no category ranked above another. Each is an Action and DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana), Wisdom (Insight), or Charisma (Persuasion). Three successes before 2 failures reprogram the ritual; failure adds a Bond Snarl hazard but does not erase other routes.
CUT: target the red core thread after one hostile action or one deliberate Cut declaration. Core Thread AC 14, 20 HP. Destroying it ends the enchantment and all magical bond effects permanently.

Initiative 20: Forced Knot. Two creatures within 30 feet make DC 13 Strength or Dexterity save; on failure they are pulled 10 feet toward one another and Restrained by a shared cord until either uses an Action to cut/free it (AC 12, 8 HP).
Directly reducing the Heartloom to 0 HP has the same consequence as Cut.

runSteps.title: Name all three routes
runSteps.text: Restore, Reweave, and Cut are visible on the loom.

runSteps.title: Center consent
runSteps.text: No route requires declaring a relationship someone does not choose.

runSteps.title: End the moment a route completes
runSteps.text: All forced cords release immediately.

scenes.advanceWhen: The Heartloom is restored, rewritten, or severed.

exitChoices.label: Restore the full pattern
exitChoices.description: Bring friendship, family, mentorship, partners, and chosen kin back to equal standing.

exitChoices.label: Rewrite the rules
exitChoices.description: Keep magic but make self-definition and opt-out explicit.

scenes.title: Resolution: Five Colors Again
scenes.readAloud: Five colors climb the bridge arches again. The cords around wrists dissolve into loose ribbons that fall harmlessly to the stones. Juniper ties a blue FRIEND ribbon beside a red PARTNER ribbon at equal height. Nobody moves it.
gmNotes: Award 160 gp total and five Rosebridge Favor ribbons.
Future festival displays give equal space to all five bond categories.
Celia remains festival chair only if she accepts the public correction.

runSteps.title: Show equal categories
runSteps.text: No bond type is treated as second class.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 160 gp and Favor ribbons.

scenes.advanceWhen: The restored festival and rewards are recorded.

scenes.title: Resolution: Name Your Own Strand
scenes.purpose: Reward keeping the magic while explicitly coding consent and self-definition.
scenes.readAloud: The old category signs fold away. New brass words appear on the Heartloom display: NAME YOUR OWN STRAND. RELEASE IS ALWAYS ALLOWED. NO STRAND ABOVE ANOTHER. The bridge relaxes with a sound like a held breath finally leaving.
gmNotes: Award 180 gp total and the Free Strand token, a story item granting advantage on one future Rosebridge check involving mediation or boundary-setting.
The festival keeps magic but stops assigning relationship categories from outside.
Opt-out becomes a formal part of the rite.

runSteps.title: Write the new rules
runSteps.text: Self-definition, release, equality.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 180 gp and Free Strand token.

scenes.advanceWhen: The rewritten rules and rewards are recorded.

scenes.title: Resolution: Ribbons Without Magic
scenes.purpose: Respect ending supernatural bond enforcement while preserving the festival as a voluntary human ritual.
scenes.readAloud: The core thread snaps. Every glowing cord becomes ordinary cloth. People untie themselves, retie ribbons where they want them, or pocket them entirely. The bridge remains standing. The festival is suddenly quieter—and far more voluntary.
gmNotes: Award 160 gp total.
The Heartloom enchantment ends permanently.
Rosebridge may keep a nonmagical ribbon festival if townsfolk choose.

runSteps.title: Release everyone immediately
runSteps.text: No lingering magical bond remains.

runSteps.title: Record reward
runSteps.text: Award 160 gp.

scenes.advanceWhen: Rewards and the future nonmagical festival are recorded.

encounters.name: Forced Festival Cords
encounters.summary: Magical ribbons bind festivalgoers under incorrect relationship labels.
encounters.resolution: Free people physically, let both parties freely name an accurate bond, or move on after clearing a path.
encounters.talkOut: The hazard responds only to the bound people's own voluntary declaration; outsiders cannot define the relationship for them.
encounters.bypass: Cut mundane festival rigging and take the archive stair, leaving Tomas to stabilize the bridge.
encounters.objective: Reach the archive while demonstrating that consent changes the magic.

encounters.resolution: Defeat them, unravel with Arcana/Sleight of Hand, or resolve the nearby relationship conflict to collapse them.
encounters.talkOut: Not sentient; they unravel automatically when the linked people freely state or reject the bond.
encounters.bypass: Move through the square along Tomas's braced path.
encounters.objective: Resolve three human bond examples and keep the bridge stable.

encounters.name: The Heartloom

encounters.resolution: Complete Restore, complete Reweave, destroy the core thread, or reduce the loom to 0 HP.
encounters.talkOut: It responds to accurate voluntary declarations and rule changes, not ordinary persuasion alone.
encounters.bypass: Restore and Reweave are complete noncombat routes.
encounters.objective: Decide how Rosebridge honors bonds without overriding the people in them.

policies: No relationship label is ever required from a person who does not choose it.
All required facts survive the absence or hostility of any one NPC.
Failure adds strain, restraint, or extra hazards but never removes all finale routes.

routes.trigger: Celia is unavailable or refuses cooperation.
routes.response: The signed transfer list, sponsor brief, and sealed archive boxes prove the exclusion policy.
Shelf labels, founder tapestry, and old display plans establish the five equal bond categories.

routes.trigger: Tomas cannot guide the underbridge route.
routes.response: A maintenance diagram on the bridge rail marks the east service stair and five category channels.
stateChanges: Consent evidence remains in the inscription.

routes.trigger: Recovered ribbon boxes are destroyed or abandoned.
routes.response: The party can use written category names and voluntary declarations instead; Restore checks lose preparation advantage but remain legal.

routes.trigger: The party skips or rushes earlier investigation and reaches the final scene without all resolution clues.
routes.response: The three shuttle handles rise with engraved labels and the floor mosaic shows all five bond categories before initiative.

routes.trigger: The party attacks the Heartloom before understanding why it is forcing bond labels.
routes.response: The Heartloom defends itself and increases structural strain, but the archive boxes, founder tapestry, consent inscription, and labeled shuttle handles still reveal Restore, Reweave, and Cut.
stateChanges: Required evidence and finale access remain available.

pathPressure.principle: Prepared social investigation reduces structural strain and preloads Restore, while rushed play preserves every ending at greater tactical pressure. The ending is never locked by skipped preparation; the party can still finish, but rushing carries the stated costs.
prepared: Sorting ribbon boxes grants advantage on the first Restore action.
Placing up to two category bundles underbridge grants prepared Restore successes.
Resolving Bond Square examples reduces STRAIN.
rushed: Skipping Bond Square starts the finale with STRAIN 2.
Ignoring underbridge channels removes prepared Restore successes.
Entering without consent proof adds one Bond Snarl on the first failed Reweave action.

cutOrder: If 25+ minutes behind, auto-reveal the five-category founder pattern in the archive.
If 15+ minutes behind in Bond Square, run two examples instead of three but include one opt-out/release case.
Never cut consent mechanics, the broad original tradition, or the three finale routes.
optionalOrder: Additional bond examples beyond the three required cases.
Founder history after the five categories are established.

creatures.name: Heartloom
creatures.trait: Core Thread: after one hostile action or Cut declaration, AC 14, 20 HP; destroying it reduces the Heartloom to 0 HP and ends the enchantment.
creatures.tactics: Use forced cords to reposition ritual actors and protect its core thread.

encounters.end: Restore succeeds, Reweave succeeds, or the Heartloom reaches 0 HP.

hazards.failure: Take 1d6 force and become Restrained until freed with an Action.
hazards.failForward: The route remains open and recovered ribbon bundles can disable zones.

hazards.trigger: Initiative count 20 while the Heartloom remains unresolved.
hazards.save: DC 13 Strength or Dexterity saving throw for two targeted creatures.
hazards.failure: Each is pulled 10 feet toward the other and Restrained by a shared cord.
hazards.failForward: Shared cords can be cut or freed with an Action and never dictate relationship status.

rewards.reward: 160 gp total and five Rosebridge Favor ribbons.
180 gp total and the Free Strand token.
160 gp total; future festival ribbons are entirely nonmagical.

flowContract.principle: One Valentine/bonds mystery: expose the narrowed tradition, demonstrate consent, reach the loom, then branch only at the final intervention.

continuity.relationshipEffect: Update Maestra Vell's Hearthford relationship state based on how the party handled this night.
continuity.standaloneRule: The adventure still runs standalone; the Hearthford frame supplies continuity but is never required to solve the plot.
